title: Individual differences supply the material for natural selection

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Individual differences supply the material for natural selection

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The slight individual differences among members of a species provide the materials that natural selection accumulates, in the same way that man accumulates individual differences in domestic productions.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These individual differences are highly important for us, as they afford materials for natural selection to accumulate, in the same manner as man can accumulate in any given direction individual differences in his domesticated productions.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter II, “Variation under Nature”; section “Individual Differences”. Scope: species in a state of nature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch02-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Heritable variation and evolutionary response are standard measurable quantities represented in many open datasets. Existing evidence spans enough systems for a strong test of the mechanism, though not every species.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure heritable within-species differences and test whether selection differentials on them predict allele-frequency or trait shifts across generations. Repeatable directional accumulation supports the mechanism; absence of heritable variation or response refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Field selection estimates can be environmentally confounded.

Well-studied taxa are nonrandom.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Barcode and sequence archives document that individuals of a species differ, for a wide taxonomic range, and a smaller literature shows those differences are often heritable. The archives themselves do not contain the selection-response test, so the mechanism is only partly in existing open tables. A result would speak to a well-studied subset and would still sit close to the definition of selection on standing variation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate heritability of ordinary within-species individual differences and the response to selection on those differences, as opposed to responses that require rare sports or new mutations. Positive heritability and a response attributable to standing individual differences would support the claim; evolution that proceeds only by rare macromutations, or individual differences that are never heritable, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The statement is close to the definition of selection on standing variation once heritability is granted.

Sequence differences are a reinterpretation of the visible individual differences Darwin treated as the raw material.

Heritability and selection response are scattered across studies and are not columns in the barcode archives.

analysis feasibility: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.4
data existence: 0.5
